name: Forza Motorsport 5
post_apply_message:
Forza Motorsport 5 (Xbox One build, run through Azimuth) is in Steam on GE-Proton 11-1. Apply keeps the shortcut's existing Steam ID, so its prefix stays attached.

The shortcut starts azimuth.exe with --game="Forza Motorsport 5" --skip-launcher. If Azimuth's launcher window opens anyway, pick Forza Motorsport 5 there.

Settings live in data/azimuth.ini inside the game folder. Change them in Azimuth's launcher: the file is UTF-16, and a text tool that rewrites it as UTF-8 breaks it.

If a capture comes back empty after a real session, the saves path in this recipe is wrong: it has not been confirmed against a real save yet.
notes:
Mirrors the handheld as it stood on 2026-11-06. Forza Motorsport 5 (the Xbox One build) runs through Azimuth, the Xbox-to-PC wrapper, under GE-Proton 11-1. The folder holds azimuth.exe (8,613,376 bytes, sha256 56d2c9cb6ccf3ae1836dee9676b64285f3a247efa2d12cf02c6c742696b3b092), byte-identical to the one in the Forza Horizon 2, Forza Horizon 3 and Forza Motorsport 6 folders. That same exe logged itself as Azimuth 1.0.4 in the Forza Horizon 3 folder on 4-5 Nov 2026 (data/logs/azimuth.log), which is where the version comes from.

WHAT CHANGED FROM THE OLD RECIPE. It used to target RaceOne5.exe (a rebranded Azimuth 0.9.9 with data/RaceOneEngine.ini) and carried an ini_edit step that kept two game_folder keys relative. None of that exists any more: the folder was rebuilt around azimuth.exe on 27 Oct 2026 and no RaceOne5 file is left. The ini_edit step is gone, and so are the RaceOne5-only claims in the old notes (its README, scene-overrides, the washed-out Career colours, the single 430-frame test run). The recipe id is unchanged on purpose.

WHAT THE RECIPE DOES: an install_runner for GE-Proton11-1 and a steam_shortcut that writes exactly what the main account holds today - appid 3452585603, exe azimuth.exe in the game folder, start dir the game folder, launch options --game="Forza Motorsport 5" --skip-launcher, compat tool GE-Proton11-1. Nothing is shipped, because there is nothing non-stock in the folder (see below).

THE APPID IS PINNED, NOT DERIVED. The recipe formula crc32("gfm:forza-motorsport-5") gives 2235397205. That was the appid of the old RaceOne5 shortcut, not the live one: the live shortcut and its prefix use 3452585603. Without the pin, Apply would rewrite the existing entry's appid to the derived one on every account, which leaves the live prefix behind and starts an empty one. steam_appid stays null: it is for real Steam installs, and detection would go looking for an appmanifest.

TWO STEAM ACCOUNTS. The shortcut exists in both accounts' shortcuts.vdf under the same appid. The main account calls it "Forza Motorsport 5" and the second account "Forza Motorsport 5 (Azimuth)". Apply writes to every account and renames the entry to the recipe name, so the second account's name is kept as an alias and its entry is matched rather than duplicated. The previous recipe name, "Forza Motorsport 5 (RaceOne5)", and the older aliases stay as aliases too, because reclaim and detection match on every name.

LAYOUT (verified on disk). The game package sits one level down in Forza_1.0.0.20_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe/ (era.vbi, Mount/, EmbeddedXvd/; 3295 files, the same count as when it was staged). azimuth.exe and data/ sit beside that folder. Forza Motorsport 6 differs: its package is at the root of its folder. Package identity from Mount/AppxManifest.xml: Name "Forza", Version 1.0.0.20, x64, TitleId 7B35D917. The game exe is Mount/forza_durango_release_final.exe, lowercase on disk although the manifest spells it mixed-case, sha256 94dad21851d335e9a33231dc2a1de2ecd4b93eefdf5f6772085bf6886bf47db7. That hash appears as a 64-hex string inside azimuth.exe (checked 2026-11-06), so Azimuth pins this exact exe and a differently packaged dump may be refused. Case matters here: the package folder name in azimuth.ini must match the directory byte for byte on a case-sensitive filesystem, and it does.

azimuth.ini IS UTF-16LE + BOM + CRLF. NEVER point ini_edit at it: ini_edit reads and writes UTF-8 and raises nothing while it misaligns every following code unit. Its launcher paths are absolute and are left exactly as they are: [launcher] game=7b35d917, and [title-7b35d917] folder=D:\Games\Forza Motorsport 5\Forza_1.0.0.20_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe. D: is the Wine drive letter for the mounted SD card (the prefix's dosdevices/d: points at the card); Wine creates it itself, so no step is needed. The file is listed in save_paths because it holds the per-game settings, and it is a plain byte-for-byte copy.

NOTHING NON-STOCK IN THE FOLDER. Compared with the Forza Motorsport 6 and Forza Horizon 3 folders on 2026-11-06: azimuth.exe, data/licenses.txt and all 22 files under data/bin hash identically, including the stock 4608-byte azimuth-tls.dll (sha256 ffa229b6c62228bf6126de6f140c6a70326c536524bec00f9304ac6591805bb7). There is no winmm.dll, DWrite.dll or Extra Options file here, unlike the Forza Horizon 2 and 3 folders. The only extra file is ISOLATION.txt (also in the Forza Motorsport 6 and Forza Horizon 3 folders): one line saying the folder has its own executable, settings and runtime, that the existing Steam app id and prefix were kept, and that no Store saves were imported. Nothing reads it, so it is not shipped.

SAVES - UNVERIFIED. {game_dir}/data/titles/7B35D917/saves does not exist yet: the title folder holds only art/ and tmp/. The path is inferred from how the Forza Horizon 2 and 3 folders lay out their saves (titles/<TITLEID>/saves/player-N/...), with the title id taken from the package manifest and written uppercase as on disk. It is the narrow form on purpose: the whole title folder would also sweep in art/ and tmp/. Capture skips a missing path silently, so an empty capture after a real session means this path is wrong - check it against the first save that appears. Azimuth keeps only the latest two save revisions on Forza Horizon 2 (not yet seen for this game), so capture early.

NO OLDER SAVE FOUND. Checked on 2026-11-06: this folder, the Azimuth update backups and the Forza Horizon 3 folder's leftover 7B35D917 directory on the handheld (art only), the staged copy of the old RaceOne5 bundle on the NAS (a pipeline log and an empty tmp), and a name search of the Windows desktop's C: and D: drives (no title folder or save; the only RaceOne/ForzaMastro files are the builder's own launcher tool). The only FM5 capture ever stored on the NAS is the old engine's settings file, which is not a save.

NOT YET CONFIRMED IN PLAY. The only sessions in data/logs/azimuth.log (27 Oct 2026, Azimuth 1.0.1) opened the launcher and quit. They report "--game=Forza Motorsport 5: no game of that name is added; the launcher opens", so --game/--skip-launcher did not skip the launcher in those runs, and nothing has been logged since. Mirrored as it is; not re-tested on 1.0.4.

THE NAS COPY IS STILL THE RACEONE5 BUNDLE. _games/Forza Motorsport 5 holds RaceOne5.exe and no azimuth.exe, so a deploy from it gives a folder whose shortcut points at nothing until the Azimuth files are copied in. Re-stage it before relying on it.

Do not confuse this with forza-motorsport-linux, which is the 2023 Forza Motorsport.
